**Mexico**,[[a]](#cite_note-11)[[b]](#cite_note-13) officially the **United Mexican States**,[[c]](#cite_note-14) is a country in [North America](/wiki/North_America "North America").[[12]](#cite_note-15) It is the northernmost country in [Latin America](/wiki/Latin_America "Latin America") and borders the [United States of America](/wiki/United_States "United States") to the north, and [Guatemala](/wiki/Guatemala "Guatemala") and [Belize](/wiki/Belize "Belize") to the southeast; while having [maritime boundaries](/wiki/Maritime_boundary "Maritime boundary") with the [Pacific Ocean](/wiki/Pacific_Ocean "Pacific Ocean") to the west, the [Caribbean Sea](/wiki/Caribbean_Sea "Caribbean Sea") to the southeast, and the [Gulf of Mexico](/wiki/Gulf_of_Mexico "Gulf of Mexico") to the east. Mexico covers 1,972,550 km2 (761,610 sq mi),[[13]](#cite_note-cia.gov-16) and is the [thirteenth-largest country](/wiki/List_of_countries_by_area "List of countries by area") in the world by land area. With a population exceeding 130 million, Mexico is the [tenth-most populous country](/wiki/List_of_countries_by_population "List of countries by population") in the world and is home to the [largest number of native Spanish speakers](/wiki/Hispanophone#Countries "Hispanophone") as of 2020.[[1]](#cite_note-2020_Census-1) [Mexico City](/wiki/Mexico_City "Mexico City") is the capital and [largest city in Mexico](/wiki/List_of_cities_in_Mexico "List of cities in Mexico"), which ranks among the [most populous metropolitan areas](/wiki/List_of_cities_by_population "List of cities by population") in the world.

Human presence in Mexico dates back to at least 8,000 BC. AlphaGo (white) won the first game. Lee appeared to be in control throughout the match, but AlphaGo gained the advantage in the final 20 minutes, and Lee resigned.[[45]](#cite_note-bbc_9_March_2016-45) Lee stated afterwards that he had made a critical error at the beginning of the match; he said that the computer's strategy in the early part of the game was "excellent" and that the AI had made one unusual move that no human Go player would have made.[[45]](#cite_note-bbc_9_March_2016-45) David Ormerod, commenting on the game at Go Game Guru, described Lee's seventh stone as "a strange move to test AlphaGo's strength in the opening", characterising the move as a mistake and AlphaGo's response as "accurate and efficient". He described AlphaGo's position as favourable in the first part of the game, considering that Lee started to come back with move 81 before making "questionable" moves at 119 and 123, followed by a "losing" move at 129.[[46]](#cite_note-Gogameguru_9_March_2016-46) Professional Go player [Cho Hanseung](/wiki/Cho_Hanseung "Cho Hanseung") commented that AlphaGo's game had greatly improved from when it beat [Fan Hui](/wiki/Fan_Hui "Fan Hui") in October 2015.[[46]](#cite_note-Gogameguru_9_March_2016-46) Michael Redmond described the computer's game as being more aggressive than against Fan.[[47]](#cite_note-47)

According to 9-dan Go grandmaster Kim Seong-ryong, Lee seemed stunned by AlphaGo's strong play on the 102nd stone.[[48]](#cite_note-hani.co.kr-48) After watching AlphaGo make the game's 102nd move, Lee mulled over his options for more than 10 minutes.[[48]](#cite_note-hani.co.kr-48)

The vain and petulant Rose in *[The Little Prince](/wiki/The_Little_Prince "The Little Prince")* was likely inspired by Saint-Exupéry's [Salvadoran](/wiki/Salvadoran "Salvadoran") wife, [Consuelo de Saint-Exupéry](/wiki/Consuelo_de_Saint-Exup%C3%A9ry "Consuelo de Saint-Exupéry").

Following the [German invasion of France in 1940](/wiki/German_invasion_of_France_in_1940 "German invasion of France in 1940"), Saint-Exupéry flew a [Bloch MB.174](/wiki/Bloch_MB.174 "Bloch MB.174") with the *Groupe de reconnaissance II/33* reconnaissance squadron of the [Armée de l'Air](/wiki/Arm%C3%A9e_de_l%27Air "Armée de l'Air").[[28]](#cite_note-30)

After [France's armistice with Germany](/wiki/Armistice_of_22_June_1940 "Armistice of 22 June 1940"), Saint-Exupéry went into exile in North America, escaping through Portugal. He stayed in [Estoril](/wiki/Estoril "Estoril"), at the Hotel Palácio, between 28 November and 20 December 1940.[[29]](#cite_note-31) He described his impressions of his stay in *Lettre à un otage*.[[30]](#cite_note-32) On the same day that he checked out, he boarded the S.S. *Siboney* and arrived in New York City on the last day of 1940,[[31]](#cite_note-33) with the intention of convincing the US to enter the conflict against Nazi Germany quickly.[[32]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTESchiff1996331-34) On 14 January 1941, at a [Hotel Astor](/wiki/Hotel_Astor "Hotel Astor") author luncheon attended by approximately 1,500, he belatedly received his [National Book Award](/wiki/National_Book_Award "National Book Award") for *[Wind, Sand and Stars](/wiki/Wind,_Sand_and_Stars "Wind, Sand and Stars")*, won a y

Documented use of the phrase "United States of America" dates back to January 2, 1776. On that day, [Stephen Moylan](/wiki/Stephen_Moylan "Stephen Moylan"), a [Continental Army](/wiki/Continental_Army "Continental Army") aide to General [George Washington](/wiki/George_Washington "George Washington"), wrote a letter to [Joseph Reed](/wiki/Joseph_Reed_(politician) "Joseph Reed (politician)"), Washington's [aide-de-camp](/wiki/Aide-de-camp "Aide-de-camp"), seeking to go "with full and ample powers from the United States of America to Spain" to seek assistance in the [Revolutionary War](/wiki/American_Revolutionary_War "American Revolutionary War") effort.[[22]](#cite_note-DeLear-20132-33)[[23]](#cite_note-34) The first known public usage is an [anonymous essay](/wiki/Anonymous_work "Anonymous work") published in the [Williamsburg](/wiki/Williamsburg,_Virginia "Williamsburg, Virginia") newspaper *[The Virginia Gazette](/wiki/The_Virginia_Gazette "The Virginia Gazette")* on April 6, 1776.[[22]](#cite_note-DeLear-20132-33) Sometime on or after June 11, 1776, [Thomas Jefferson](/wiki/Thomas_Jefferson "Thomas Jefferson") wrote "United States of America" in a rough draft of the [Declaration of Independence](/wiki/United_States_Declaration_of_Independence "United States Declaration of Independence"),[[22]](#cite_note-DeLear-20132-33) which was adopted by the [Second Continental Congress](/wiki/Second_Continental_Congress "Second Continental Congress") on July 4, 1776.[[24]](#cite_note-Davis72-35)

Charles at the Flint National Eisteddfod, several days after his [investiture as the Prince of Wales](/wiki/Investiture_of_Charles,_Prince_of_Wales "Investiture of Charles, Prince of Wales").

Charles was created [Prince of Wales](/wiki/Prince_of_Wales "Prince of Wales") and [Earl of Chester](/wiki/Earl_of_Chester "Earl of Chester") on 26 July 1958,[[30]](#cite_note-37) although [his investiture](/wiki/Investiture_of_Charles,_Prince_of_Wales "Investiture of Charles, Prince of Wales") did not take place until 1 July 1969, when he was crowned by his mother in a televised ceremony at [Caernarfon Castle](/wiki/Caernarfon_Castle "Caernarfon Castle").[[31]](#cite_note-38) The [event was controversial](/wiki/Controversy_of_the_Prince_of_Wales_title "Controversy of the Prince of Wales title") in Wales amid rising [Welsh nationalist](/wiki/Welsh_nationalist "Welsh nationalist") sentiment.[[32]](#cite_note-39) He [took his seat](/wiki/Introduction_(House_of_Lords) "Introduction (House of Lords)") in the [House of Lords](/wiki/House_of_Lords "House of Lords") the following year,[[33]](#cite_note-40) delivering his [maiden speech](/wiki/Maiden_speech "Maiden speech") on 13 June 1974,[[34]](#cite_note-41) the first royal to speak from the floor since the future [Edward VII](/wiki/Edward_VII "Edward VII") in 1884.[[35]](#cite_note-42) He addressed the House again in 1975.[[36]](#cite_note-43)

Charles increasingly undertook public duties, founding [the Prince's Trust](/wiki/The_Prince%27s_Trust "The Prince's Trust") in 1976[[37]](#cite_note-44) and travelling to the United States in 1981.[

Studio executives were already contemplating sequels to *Homecoming* before the original film's release.[[119]](#cite_note-120)[[120]](#cite_note-121) The filmmakers developed *Spider-Man: Far From Home* as the final film of the [third phase](/wiki/Marvel_Cinematic_Universe:_Phase_Three "Marvel Cinematic Universe: Phase Three") of the MCU's Infinity Saga.[[121]](#cite_note-122)[[122]](#cite_note-123) Watts and screenwriters [Chris McKenna](/wiki/Chris_McKenna_(writer) "Chris McKenna (writer)") and [Erik Sommers](/wiki/Erik_Sommers "Erik Sommers") were confirmed to be returning for the film in mid 2017.[[123]](#cite_note-124)[[124]](#cite_note-McKennaSommers-125) Watts was especially interested in resolving the narratives about the Spider-Man characters from *[Avengers: Endgame](/wiki/Avengers:_Endgame "Avengers: Endgame")* (2019) because they received an ambiguous resolution.[[125]](#cite_note-126) In *Far From Home*, [Nick Fury](/wiki/Nick_Fury_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe) "Nick Fury (Marvel Cinematic Universe)") ([Samuel L. Jackson](/wiki/Samuel_L._Jackson "Samuel L. Jackson")) recruits Peter to help [Mysterio](/wiki/Mysterio_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe) "Mysterio (Marvel Cinematic Universe)") ([Jake Gyllenhaal](/wiki/Jake_Gyllenhaal "Jake Gyllenhaal")) defeat the [Elementals](/wiki/Elementals_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe) "Elementals (Marvel Cinematic Universe)"). Filming occurred from July to October 2018,[[126]](#cite_note-127)[[127]](#cite_note-128) and the theatrical release was scheduled in July 2019.[[128]](#cite_note-129) *Far From Home* became the first Spider-Man film to gross $1 billion at the box office.[[129]](#cite_note-BillionTheWrap-130)
